item.text: The targeted search recovered a stronger route through contemporaneous government and intergovernmental records. The most useful additions are: a September 2000 U.S. report tying Kim’s leadership to military-first resource allocation and recording the unresolved capability risk; a Japanese defense-ministry review with page-level discussion of Kim’s economic guidance, the 2000 budget, centralized economic control, and food shortfall; a June 2000 Amnesty record with target-period welfare and security findings; and the DPRK’s own 2000 rights submission as qualified contrary evidence. I’m now separating direct Kim attribution from institutional/context claims and excluding post-period or derivative material.

I recovered six defensible additions and one rejected candidate. The sandbox remained read-only, so I could not persist `research-materials.md` or `research-ledger-manifest.json`.

Added units:

- `EVID-CONT-009` — Japan NIDS, *East Asian Strategic Review 2000*, pp. 149–151. Kim Jong-Il’s military-first governance, April 2000 SPA budget, and economic-priority framing. Links: 4B, 5B, 8B. Attribution: direct for Kim’s policy posture; institutional for implementation. [Source](https://www.nids.mod.go.jp/english/publication/east-asian/pdf/2000/east-asian_e2000_5.pdf)

- `EVID-CONT-010` — NIDS, pp. 151–152. DPRK’s 2000 centralized National Economy Plan law and continuing military role in economic activity. Links: 5B.4, 5B.7, 8B.2, 8B.6. Attribution: institutional; not proof of Kim’s personal decision. [Source](https://www.nids.mod.go.jp/english/publication/east-asian/pdf/2000/east-asian_e2000_5.pdf)

- `EVID-CONT-011` — NIDS, p. 150. FAO estimated a 1.29-million-ton grain shortage for November 1999–October 2000 and deemed international assistance indispensable. Links: 5B.3, 5B.8, 5B.9, 6B.1, 6B.6. Attribution: country-level context only. [Source](https://www.nids.mod.go.jp/english/publication/east-asian/pdf/2000/east-asian_e2000_5.pdf)

- `EVID-CONT-012` — U.S. 2000 Report to Congress, lines 75–83. Kim was described as firmly in control; resources were directed toward military/security priorities while food, energy, infrastructure, and foreign-exchange shortages persisted. Links: 4B, 5B, 8B. Attribution: direct leadership assessment, but report-level inference rather than a personal order. Contrary evidence: limited markets and private agriculture were permitted. [Source](https://www.globalsecurity.org/wmd/library/news/dprk/2000/korea09122000.html)

- `EVID-CONT-013` — NIDS, pp. 176–177. September 2000 Berlin talks produced a conditional North Korean commitment not to test long-range missiles while talks continued; the same review records unresolved nuclear and missile-development suspicions. Links: 8B.6, 8B.7; contrary evidence for 1B/2B. Attribution: institutional, not personal. [Source](https://www.nids.mod.go.jp/english/publication/east-asian/pdf/2000/east-asian_e2000_5.pdf)

- `EVID-CONT-014` — Amnesty International Report 2000, dated 1 June 2000. Food crisis, child malnutrition, vulnerability, border shootings, beatings, and prison-camp risks were reported; access and information remained tightly controlled. Links: 5B, 6B, 7B. Attribution: institutional/security-system evidence, not a Kim-specific order. [Source](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/amnesty/2000/en/16912)
